summary.coreFinding: After Leads, Customers, and CEO/Admin Staff moved away from normal Social startup ownership, social-app.js is still dominated by route/session startup, public menu/QR/cart/order wiring, Feed/Search/Map bridge wiring, overlay/modal orchestration, and remaining Social-owned staff/businessAccounts paths.
summary.recommendedNextStepTitle: Public menu / QR / business profile lightweight entry

missingOrNotApplicable.apps/menyra-social/core/search: No dedicated core/search directory exists; search is currently coupled through app-shell, discovery, feed, and map helpers.

evidence: social-app.js still owns route canonicalization, startup snapshot glue, pending protected route handling, and active tab synchronization.
session-data-runtime-controller.js and public-bootstrap-runtime-controller.js still depend on menu/cart/search/map/profile state during session changes.
biggestRemainingCouplings.auditConclusion: Largest raw coupling, but not the safest next extraction because it crosses every product surface.

biggestRemainingCouplings.area: Public menu, QR, cart, orders, business profile entry
evidence: social-app.js imports createMenuPublicRuntimeController and createTableQrRuntimeController directly.
social-app.js keeps shopCart, orders, menuDetail, tableQr state and unsub holders.
orders-runtime-controller.js is lazy, but menu/QR/cart state and public profile entry are still loaded through normal Social startup wiring.
biggestRemainingCouplings.auditConclusion: Best next real slimming target because the surface is large, route-scoped, and mostly separable from Feed/Search/Map and Chat.

evidence: app-controller-bridge.js dynamically imports discovery-runtime-controller.js, but social-app.js still passes scoreSearchMatch, search state, renderSearchView, renderMapView, refreshSearchView, ensureLeafletLoaded, cleanupLeaflet, and buildRestaurantLocations through bridge bindings.
Heart write adapter still imports discovery-runtime-controller.js for Leaflet support.
biggestRemainingCouplings.auditConclusion: High benefit but higher risk because Feed/Search/Map are core Social behavior.

evidence: social-app.js imports overlay root, overlay render, overlay bind, basic overlay, chat/post overlay, menu/focus overlay, and menu detail overlay helpers.
social-app.js still owns modal escape state, overlay cache, post modal unsub holders, and menu detail unsub holders.
biggestRemainingCouplings.auditConclusion: Good cleanup candidate after public route ownership is clearer, but runtime startup benefit is lower than public menu/QR separation.

evidence: Bare /staff remains Social and still requires loadCeoStaff, renderStaffView, bindCrmStaffEventsCore, and saveCeoStaffFromViewCore wiring.
businessAccounts remains Social and still requires loadBusinessAccounts, renderBusinessAccountsView, and bindBusinessAccountsEvents wiring.
Heart has CRM admin shell consumer/read/write support for staff and businessAccounts, but route ownership is not equivalent to Social businessAccounts ownership.
biggestRemainingCouplings.auditConclusion: Not the best next slimming block until the bare /staff and businessAccounts ownership decisions are explicit.

remainingSocialStaffRemnantsNotSafeToRem: apps/menyra-social/social-app.js passes renderStaffView and loadCeoStaff through shell/runtime clusters for bare /staff.
apps/menyra-social/core/app-shell/shell-ui-runtime-cluster.js still renders staff and businessAccounts views.
apps/menyra-social/core/app-events/app-events-main-bind-utils.js still gates bindCrmStaffEventsCore to the current staff tab.
sharedCrmCoreNotSafeToRemove: apps/menyra-social/core/crm/* remains shared by Social staff runtime and Heart CRM admin adapters.
apps/menyra-social/core/leads/* remains shared by Heart CRM import/read/write paths.
Heart imports Social CRM staff save helpers through heart-crm-admin-write-adapter.js.
remainingCrmAndStaffCoupling.whyNotNext: The next Staff/CRM deletion point depends on a product decision for bare /staff and staff.mnyra.com. Removing more now risks restaurant staff or business staff behavior.

businessAccountsStatus.status: Still Social-owned for normal app behavior.
evidence: apps/menyra-social/core/business-accounts/business-accounts-runtime-controller.js remains active.
social-app.js still wires loadBusinessAccounts, renderBusinessAccountsView, and bindBusinessAccountsEvents.
shell-dom-runtime-controller.js still exposes the businessAccounts drawer entry labeled Staff for business owners.
Heart state and CRM admin shell consumer know about businessAccounts, but that does not make normal Social businessAccounts safe to move.
businessAccountsStatus.dependencyDecisionNeeded: Decide whether businessAccounts should become Heart-owned and how business owner staff management maps to restaurant staff, waiter, kitchen, and staff.mnyra.com behavior.

publicMenuQrStatus.status: Large and route-scoped; best next slimming block.
evidence: social-app.js imports public menu and table QR controllers directly.
social-app.js owns shopCart, orders, menuDetail, and tableQr state even when the user is entering normal Social Feed/Search/Map.

profile-business-menu-runtime-cluster.js, public-bootstrap-runtime-controller.js, menu-public-runtime-controller.js, table-qr-runtime-controller.js, orders-runtime-controller.js, public profile runtime/controllers, and profile menu focus rendering form a separable route surface.
Orders controller is already lazy, which gives a pattern for deeper public route isolation.
publicMenuQrStatus.recommendedShape: Define a lightweight public business/menu entry that owns QR/menu/business profile public bootstrapping and only attaches cart/orders/menu detail when the active route needs it.
keepUnchanged: Firebase paths and order payload shapes

feedSearchMapStatus.status: Already partially lazy; still tightly wired into app-shell and Social identity.
evidence: discovery-runtime-controller.js is dynamically imported by app-controller-bridge.js.
social-app.js still passes discovery bindings for renderSearchView, renderMapView, refreshSearchView, buildRestaurantLocations, ensureLeafletLoaded, cleanupLeaflet, and scoreSearchMatch.
Feed view orchestration is large and search/location behavior crosses feed startup, map cleanup, business location state, and profile opening.
Heart imports discovery-runtime-controller.js for Leaflet support in heart-crm-admin-write-adapter.js.
feedSearchMapStatus.whyLater: The benefit is real, but Feed/Search/Map are core Social surfaces and should not be the next move without focused route/interaction tests.

overlayModalStatus.status: Cleanup candidate with moderate social-app.js impact.
evidence: social-app.js still owns overlayCache, modalEscapeBound, modalPostDocUnsub, modalLikesUnsub, modalCommentsUnsub, menuDetailDocUnsub, menuDetailLikesUnsub, and menuDetailCommentsUnsub.
social-app.js still imports and passes seven overlay bind/render helpers into bridge-shell-runtime-cluster.js.
overlay-orchestration-controller.js already exists, but ownership is not fully moved there.
overlayModalStatus.whyNotRecommendedFirst: It would reduce social-app.js wiring, but it would not unload as much startup behavior as separating public menu/QR.

authStartupStatus.status: Largest raw coupling and highest blast radius.
evidence: social-app.js still contains route canonicalization helpers, post-login routing, protected route pending state, auth bootstrap glue, and session cluster wiring.
session-data-runtime-controller.js remains a large cross-surface reset/load controller for feed, search, map, menu, staff, businessAccounts, and orders state.
public-bootstrap-runtime-controller.js still translates public route entry into Social startup state.
authStartupStatus.whyLater: Startup simplification should follow public route isolation and unresolved Staff/businessAccounts route decisions.

candidateNextSteps.title: businessAccounts to Heart
candidateNextSteps.whatItRemovesOrSeparates: Moves businessAccounts read/render/event ownership away from Social and removes the businessAccounts Social drawer/tab plumbing after route ownership is decided.
candidateNextSteps.expectedSocialAppJsImpact: Medium direct impact, roughly 40-90 direct lines plus follow-up app-shell dependency cleanup.
candidateNextSteps.expectedRuntimeImpact: Modest normal Social startup reduction; bigger conceptual benefit if Staff ownership becomes fully Heart-owned.
dependencies: Explicit product decision that businessAccounts is Heart-owned.
Verified mapping for business owner Staff, restaurant staff, waiter, kitchen, and staff.mnyra.com.
Heart route and permission contract for businessAccounts.
candidateNextSteps.whyNowOrWhyLater: Later. businessAccounts remains Social by current instruction and is entangled with business owner staff behavior.

candidateNextSteps.title: Public menu / QR / business profile lightweight entry
candidateNextSteps.whatItRemovesOrSeparates: Separates public business profile, menu, QR, cart, order, and menu-detail bootstrapping from normal Social startup so public routes load a route-specific runtime instead of the full Social shell wiring.
candidateNextSteps.expectedSocialAppJsImpact: High staged impact, roughly 150-300 lines from social-app.js over implementation plus smaller follow-up removals from bridge/controller deps.
candidateNextSteps.expectedRuntimeImpact: High for public menu/QR entry and useful for normal Social startup by avoiding public menu/cart/order setup until needed.
dependencies: Preserve current public route shapes including /casarita/menu and QR/table query variants.
Keep menu, cart, order, QR, and public profile Firestore paths and payloads unchanged.
Preserve restaurant owner menu admin behavior and public business profile entry behavior.
candidateNextSteps.whyNowOrWhyLater: Now. It is the largest route-scoped block left after CRM cleanup and does not require moving businessAccounts, bare /staff, Feed/Search/Map, or Chat.

candidateNextSteps.title: Feed/Search/Map lazy split
candidateNextSteps.whatItRemovesOrSeparates: Moves remaining discovery/search/map bridge dependencies and Feed view wiring behind a dedicated lazy Social discovery/feed runtime boundary.
candidateNextSteps.expectedSocialAppJsImpact: Medium to high, roughly 80-160 lines from social-app.js plus app-shell bridge simplification.
candidateNextSteps.expectedRuntimeImpact: Medium. Discovery is already dynamically imported, so the main gain is cleaner wiring and less normal startup coupling.
candidateNextSteps.whyNowOrWhyLater: Later. It touches core Social behavior and should follow a smaller public-route extraction.

candidateNextSteps.title: Overlay/modal cleanup
candidateNextSteps.whatItRemovesOrSeparates: Moves modal state accessors, overlay cache, modal escape state, and modal/menu-detail unsubscribe ownership out of social-app.js into an overlay runtime owner.
candidateNextSteps.expectedRuntimeImpact: Low to medium. Cleaner ownership and fewer root-level globals, but limited route startup savings.
dependencies: Overlay keyboard escape and body modal-open sync
candidateNextSteps.whyNowOrWhyLater: Good fallback if implementation must stay purely internal. Later than public menu/QR because it has less product-loading payoff.

candidateNextSteps.title: Auth/startup simplification
candidateNextSteps.whatItRemovesOrSeparates: Consolidates route canonicalization, auth restore, pending protected routes, startup snapshots, and session data reset/load orchestration into a thinner startup owner.
candidateNextSteps.expectedSocialAppJsImpact: High, roughly 150-300 lines from social-app.js if done in stages.
candidateNextSteps.expectedRuntimeImpact: Potentially high, but uncertain until route-specific public startup and Staff/businessAccounts ownership are resolved.
candidateNextSteps.whyNowOrWhyLater: Later. It is the largest raw coupling but the least forgiving next step.

candidateNextSteps.title: Staff route final decision
candidateNextSteps.whatItRemovesOrSeparates: Decides whether bare /staff and staff.mnyra.com remain Social forever, move to Heart, or split by role, then removes the losing ownership path.
candidateNextSteps.expectedSocialAppJsImpact: Medium after decision, roughly 50-120 lines plus CRM event/render cleanup.
candidateNextSteps.expectedRuntimeImpact: Low to medium for normal Social startup; high clarity benefit for CRM ownership.
dependencies: restaurant staff, waiter, and kitchen flows
candidateNextSteps.whyNowOrWhyLater: Later. Current instruction explicitly keeps /staff Social and forbids breaking staff.mnyra.com, waiter, kitchen, or restaurant staff flows.

candidateNextSteps.title: Shared CRM core relocation
candidateNextSteps.whatItRemovesOrSeparates: Moves shared CRM/leads helpers to a neutral shared package or Heart-owned module while preserving import contracts.
candidateNextSteps.expectedSocialAppJsImpact: Low. Mostly import-path organization, not direct normal startup slimming.
dependencies: Heart imports of Social CRM helpers
Heart imports of discovery Leaflet helpers
No Firebase path or payload changes
candidateNextSteps.whyNowOrWhyLater: Later. It is architectural cleanup, not the next best social-app.js slimming block.

recommendedNextStep.title: Public menu / QR / business profile lightweight entry
recommendedNextStep.recommendation: Choose the public menu/QR/business profile route surface as the next real slimming/refactor block.
whyBest: It is the largest actionable route-scoped coupling remaining after CRM cleanup.
It avoids changing current /staff, businessAccounts, Feed/Search/Map, Chat, waiter, kitchen, and restaurant staff behavior.
It can be staged by first introducing a public-route entry/runtime boundary, then moving cart/orders/menu-detail attachment behind that boundary.
It should reduce both social-app.js size and normal Social startup coupling more than overlay-only cleanup.
implementationGuardrails: Do not change public route shapes.
Do not change Firebase paths, query shapes, payloads, cart keys, or order writes.
Do not touch businessAccounts, bare /staff, waiter, kitchen, Chat, Feed/Search/Map, vercel.json, sw.js, or service worker behavior.
Keep restaurant owner menu admin behavior intact.

expectedBenefit.socialAppJsSlimming: Expected 150-300 lines removed from social-app.js over a staged implementation, with further follow-up simplification in app-shell/controller deps.
expectedBenefit.runtimeBenefit: Public menu and QR routes can avoid normal Social shell startup work, while normal Feed/Search/Map startup can avoid public menu/cart/order setup until required.
expectedBenefit.ownershipBenefit: Creates a clearer boundary between public business/menu entry and authenticated Social shell behavior.
expectedBenefit.maintenanceBenefit: Reduces high-volume dependency passing for menu, QR, cart, orders, menu detail, and public business profile bootstrapping.

riskList.risk: Public menu, QR, cart, or order routes regress because route parsing and startup state are currently shared with Social bootstrap.
riskList.mitigation: Keep route shapes and Firebase contracts unchanged; extract behind compatibility adapters first.

riskList.risk: Restaurant owner menu admin behavior regresses because admin menu and public menu share profile/menu focus rendering helpers.
riskList.mitigation: Do not move admin menu writes in the first step; only isolate public entry/runtime attachment.

riskList.risk: Cart persistence or guest order lookup changes accidentally.
riskList.mitigation: Preserve shopCartKey, guest order session keys, and order payload shapes exactly.

riskList.risk: Overlay/menu-detail comments and likes lose live unsubscribe cleanup.
riskList.mitigation: Keep menuDetail unsub ownership explicit until the public route runtime owns it fully.

riskList.risk: Business profile public entry affects Feed/Search/Map profile opening.
riskList.mitigation: Keep normal profile modal/profile opening paths untouched; scope extraction to public route entry.

filesNotToTouch: Firebase rules, indexes, path constants, query shapes, and payload builders
manualTestChecklist: Orders view and guest order result behavior work.
Restaurant owner menu admin still works.
Public business profile entry still works.
